Insura
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant - claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 26.2.2020 passed in MACC/78/2017 by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Harda for enhancement of the compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The Court fee of Rs.25,000/- has been paid.
2. The case of the appellant, in short, is that on 22.10.2016 at about 12.30 o'clock the appellant was standing in front of his house.

At the same time, White Car No.M.P.-47 C.A. 1082, which was driven rashly and negligently dashed against the appellant due to which he sustained serious injuries on his right leg, right shoulder, right side of stomach, left hand and near the left eye.
His primary treatment was done at Harda.
After that he was referred to Hospital at Indore.
The treatment at Indore was continued.
Due to serious injuries, his right hand has become senseless.
After that he was treated by the Doctors of Nagpur, Mumbai and Bhopal.
He spent about Rs.5 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55488 2 MA-2245-2020 lacs in his treatment.
His left hand has not been fully cured till now.

3. On filing the claim case, learned claims tribunal has awarded Rs.2,19,000/- after deducting 25%
amount towards contributory negligence from the total compensation of Rs.2,92,000/-.
The tribunal observed that the claimant was 36 years of age at the time of accident.

He sustained 60%

1 disability as per disability certificate (Ex.P-68) by the Medical Board but learned Tribunal taking the disability on different parts of his body as 15% has calculated the amount of compensation.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has relied on the decision in the case of Khamchand Sahu Vs.

Deepak Kumar Sahu and others reported in 2024 SCC OnLine MP 893, in which, in an motor accident case for a permanent disability the Coordinate bench of this court took loss of income @
50% and looking to the 28 years of age of the claimant, applied the multiplier of 17 and in the facts and circumstances of the case granted compensation of Rs.1653,181/- .

5. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 3 - Insurance Company at the time of arguments has relied on the judgment of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 and submits that as per Para 15 of the judgment Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that when permanent disability on part of the body is 45%, loss of future earning would not be 45% and took loss of earning at 20% and accordingly, calculation was done and compensation has been awarded.
6. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties.
7. Perused the statement of Tulsiram (PW-1) and the documents exhibited by him from Ex.P-1 to P-68.

sentences.text: In Paragraph -10 of cross - examination, he made statement contrary to his claim application as in claim application he has stated that he was standing on the road near his house whereas in claim case during cross-examination has stated that he was crossing the road when the accident had taken place.

Also perused the statements of Applicant witness no. 2-Girija wife of the claimant and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55488 3 MA-2245-2020 Applicant's Witness no. 3 - Dr. Kapil Patel, who has verified the disability.
8. It is seen that learned tribunal under the head of permanent disability i.e. fracture has awarded Rs.1,62,000/-.
On the date of accident, as per minimum wage notification in the State of M.P. the income was Rs.6950/- per month.
Therefore, annual income of the applicant would be Rs.6950 x 12 = Rs.83,400/-.
On adding 40% towards future prospectus, the amount becomes Rs.11,6,760/-.
Applicable multiplier in this case would be 15.
In Para -18 of the award, loss of income is has been taken at 15%, which is not proper, therefore, loss of income is taken at 20%.

Accordingly,
Rs.1,16,760/- divided by 5.
Accordingly, loss of income would be Rs.350280 = (11760x20/100x15).
For medical expenses Rs.1 lac has been awarded, which is maintained.
For pain and suffering only Rs.10,000/- has been awarded by the learned tribunal, which is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.

Similarly under the head of special diet and transportation charges the amount is enhanced from Rs.10,000/-
to Rs.50,000/-.

Under the head of expenses of Attendant, no amount has been awarded, therefore,
Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head of attendant.
For future medical expenses no amount is awarded,
Therefore, under the medical expenses head, Rs.150,000/- is awarded under this head.
For fracture Rs.1 lac is awarded.

Future loss of income Rs.350280/-
 Medical Expenses Rs.1,00,000/-
 Pain and Suffering Rs.50,000/-
